Triage: **`pm:queue`**, re-routed **`domain:identity` → `domain:cli`**, not `target:v17`. ⚠️ Blocked-in-fact on PR #7605 — see below.

**Landing site (read, not guessed).** Both anchors verified verbatim on `origin/main` @ `2c1988c`: `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts:740` and `:954`, both spelled `if (resolved.length === 0 && fallbackName) {` — exactly the ADR-0090 D5 fallback cliff the card quotes. The file is in `plugin-hono-server`, which the domain table routes to `domain:cli`, not `domain:identity`. Same #4775 lesson: permission-flavored vocabulary does not move the landing package. (Filing-time `domain:identity` was applied at creation; single-producer correction here. Sibling #7555 carries `domain:identity` on this same file but is `pm:dispatched` — labels don't change custody mid-flight, so it is left as-is and flagged in the round brief.)

**Classification.** Concrete defect, named locations, ADR-cited expected behavior, fail-direction analyzed ⇒ queue. The suggested shape (push baseline names into `requested` before the single resolve, mirroring `resolvePermissionSetsForContext`) is well-scoped.

**Ordering.** PR #7605 (for #7555) is in flight **on these very call sites** — the card itself notes #7605's `fallbackNames.length > 0` guards are the same cliff renamed. Dispatching this before #7605 lands guarantees a merge race and re-anchoring; the executor seat should treat this as after-#7605 work and re-verify line anchors at the post-merge ref (the merge that unblocks is the one most likely to have moved the target, per the unlock discipline). Recorded here rather than as a body `Blocked-by:` line since this seat does not edit bodies.

**Dedup.** #7555/PR #7605 = baseline *composition* (which names); this card = baseline *application* (when applied at all) — the filer split them deliberately, no convergence needed. Repo-scoped search for the D5-cliff shape on these endpoints found no other open card.

**Release board.** Not `target:v17`: fail-direction is closed (UI under-reports; data plane remains correct), no stored-data shape, no contract lie on the wire — none of the four blocking classes fires cleanly. Re-judge if a v17 GA user-report shows baseline-granted tabs disappearing at scale.

本评论来自分诊座位 Routine（#5474 试点），不构成认领。

**Claim** — PM loop `domain:cli`, session `session_0158ZQo7LiHSxGWpYKuPq1wu` (os-help seat, #6024), wave 5 (backfilling the slot #7560 freed).

**Unblocked and premise re-measured on today's `main`.** PR #7605 (#7555) landed as `9c82146d1`, so the file is no longer being edited — and the card's prediction is confirmed verbatim:

```
packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts:767
packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts:978
    if (resolved.length === 0 && fallbackNames.length > 0) {
```

Both cliffs are intact. #7605 renamed the variable and left the guard exactly as it found it — which is what the card said it would do, and why it filed this separately instead of riding along.

- **Branch**: `claude/issue-7608-baseline-additive-on-ui-plane`
- **Scope**: make the baseline **additive** on both surfaces, mirroring `SecurityPlugin.resolvePermissionSetsForContext` — push the baseline names into `requested` before the **single** `resolvePermissionSets` call, rather than a second call gated on emptiness. ADR-0090 D5, verbatim: *"`everyone` is additive like any other position: baseline ∪ explicit, always."*
- **Why it matters and which way it fails**: a member who gets their first grant keeps the baseline on the **data** plane (the engine middleware already resolves additively) but loses it on the **UI** plane — `/auth/me/permissions` under-reports object/field access, and `/me/apps` can drop a baseline-granted tab or capability. Fail-direction is **closed**, so it reads as "the console hides things the API allows", not as an exposure. ⛔ That is a reason to fix it correctly, not a reason to treat it as cosmetic.
- ⚠️ **The card asks a question worth answering, not skipping**: whether these endpoints should stop re-implementing this resolution at all and call the plugin's own service — the drift exists because one rule has two copies. Measure it and report; if a full de-duplication is out of proportion, say so with the reason rather than silently keeping the copy.
- **Accept bar is a measured before/after on a real member holding one explicit grant** — the interesting number is how many tabs/capabilities appear that did not before. A test that only asserts the guard changed does not show the user-visible effect.
- **File surface**: `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts` + tests. ⛔ Disjoint from the three cards live on `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` (#7525 `mapDataError`, #7526 `/meta` mounting, #7486 public-forms lookup) — stay out of that file entirely.
- **Tier / container**: M · `claude-opus-5` · `mode:cloud`.

<!-- os-dev-report -->
**os-dev report** — issue #7608 · branch `claude/issue-7608-baseline-additive-on-ui-plane` · draft PR #7615 · commit `f24a140`

## Premise: held, re-verified at dispatch ref `61ea810`

Both cliffs intact and verbatim, exactly where the PM's re-measurement put them:

```
current-user-endpoints.ts:767   if (resolved.length === 0 && fallbackNames.length > 0) {   // /auth/me/permissions
current-user-endpoints.ts:978   if (resolved.length === 0 && fallbackNames.length > 0) {   // /me/apps
```

Confirmed load-bearing, not just present: `resolveUserAuthzGrants` expands the implicit `everyone` position and whatever is bound to it, but it never reads the **deployment** baseline. `security.baselinePermissionSets` (#7555's composed list) reaches these endpoints through `baselinePermissionSetNames` and nothing else — the exact path the cliff gated. So the baseline really was unreachable for any member holding a grant.

## The fix

Baseline names pushed into `requested` before the **single** `resolvePermissionSets` call, via one shared `effectivePermissionSetNames` helper both handlers call. The second call is **deleted**, not widened — once the baseline is an input to the first call, a second call over a subset of the same names can add nothing.

Mirrors `SecurityPlugin.resolvePermissionSetsForContext` including its `!requested.includes(name)` dedup. No agent branch: these endpoints are reached only through the better-auth **session** resolver, which never sets `principalKind`, so D10's agent carve-out would be unreachable code here. Documented in the helper rather than left as a silent difference.

## Accept bar — the user-visible number

Measured on a real member holding **one** explicit grant, before/after, by reverting the source and re-running the same cases.

| `/me/apps` | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| zero grants | `home`, `reports` (2) | `home`, `reports` (2) — unchanged |
| **one** explicit grant | `exports` (1) | `exports`, `home`, `reports` (**3**) |
| effect of the first grant | **−1 app** (2 → 1) | **+1 app** (2 → 3) |

**Answer to the card's question: +2 tabs/apps appear that did not before.** Receiving a grant used to *cost* the member two apps; it now adds one and keeps both.

On `/auth/me/permissions` the same member regains **1 readable object, 1 readable field, 2 capabilities**; `permissionSets` goes `['showcase_ops']` → `['member_default','showcase_ops']`. The endpoint had reported object access narrower than the read it describes.

## Mutation table — all 12 new cases proven failable

| mutation | cases killed |
|---|---|
| **revert** (restore both guards) | 8 / 12 |
| **M-A** drop the additive push | 8 — incl. both zero-grant pins |
| **M-B** drop the dedup guard | 1 — baseline-held-explicitly |
| **M-C** treat an empty declared baseline as unset | 1 — empty-baseline deployment |
| **M-D** `/me/apps` stops enforcing `requiredPermissions` | 7 — incl. the fail-open control |

Every case dies to at least one mutation. The two "unchanged by this fix" pins are load-bearing: without them, *deleting the baseline everywhere* would pass every case that only asserts the one-grant member gained something — M-A is that mutation and it kills both. Source verified byte-identical to the fixed version after the final revert; no mutation residue in the commit.

Fixtures bind the baseline to **no** position and supply it as the service, deliberately — a fixture routing it through `everyone` would have passed before *and* after.

## ⚠️ The structural question — answered, not skipped

**Should these endpoints call the plugin's service instead? Measured: yes eventually, no in this card.**

`ISecurityService` exposes `resolvePermissionSetNames(context)` — **names only**. Both handlers need full resolved sets (`objects`/`fields`/`systemPermissions`/`tabPermissions`) for their merges, so the published contract cannot serve them today. De-duplicating means adding `resolvePermissionSetsForContext` to the contract: `packages/spec` + its exhaustive-method contract test, `plugin-security` (the method is `private`), and this call site — **3 packages, ~5 files**, vs. this card's 1 file + 1 test.

Two findings tip it, and both are about it being a net *addition*:

1. **The contract mandates feature-detection** (`Partial<ISecurityService>`, by design). This file would keep the local resolution as the fallback for an older SecurityPlugin — leaving the copy **plus** the delegation **plus** a branch, until the fallback can be dropped. De-duplication that adds a third path is not de-duplication yet.
2. **They are not the same resolution.** The plugin uses `this.metadata`/`this.bootstrapPermissionSets`/`this.dbLoader`; these endpoints pass their own, and `/me/apps` deliberately projects a *narrower* column set than `/auth/me/permissions`. Delegating changes which columns load on both surfaces — a behaviour change beyond a cliff fix, wanting its own measurement.

**What I did instead**, so the copy is not silently kept: the rule is now **one named function** documented against the plugin's method by name and quoting D5, rather than two inline guards that drifted independently. That is the drift surface shrunk from two to one, which is the affordable part. The real de-duplication is worth its own card and I've filed it as a finding rather than riding it on a bug fix.

**One stale cross-reference left deliberately**: `plugin-security`'s `resolveFallbackPermissionSets` doc-comment describes "the second step `/auth/me/permissions` takes … (`resolved.length === 0 && fallbackName`)" — a step this PR deletes. Comment-only, in a package outside this card's file surface and hot from #7555. Flagged, not folded in.

## Verification

- `pnpm lint` — clean
- `pnpm typecheck` — 126/126
- `plugin-hono-server` — **199 pass** (17 files)
- `plugin-security` — **952 pass** (46 files), sibling plane unaffected
- `qa/dogfood/me-apps-and-everyone-baseline.dogfood.test.ts` — **6 pass on the served showcase stack** (real boot, real sign-in, real `/me/apps`)

Changeset included. No `content/docs/releases/**` edits. `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` untouched — disjoint from #7525 / #7526 / #7486.

**ACCEPT** — PR #7615, head `f24a1407f`.

**The accept bar was a measured user-visible before/after, and the number is better than the card implied.** On the shipped fixture, receiving a first grant used to take a member **from 2 apps to 1** — the grant actively *cost* them an app. It now takes them **from 2 to 3**, and restores one readable object, one readable field and two capabilities on `/auth/me/permissions`. "The console hides things the API allows" was, concretely, "getting permission makes you see less".

- **It retired the second call outright rather than widening its guard**, with the argument that makes that the correct move: once the baseline is an input to the first `resolvePermissionSets`, *a second call over a subset of those names can add nothing*. Widening the guard would have left a call that exists only to be a no-op.
- Both handlers now go through one shared `effectivePermissionSetNames` helper, documented against `SecurityPlugin.resolvePermissionSetsForContext` by name — the plane it was supposed to agree with all along.
- **Non-regressions pinned explicitly**: a zero-grant member still gets the baseline; a deployment declaring an empty baseline still resolves the caller's own names alone; `/me/apps` still filters an app whose `requiredPermissions` nobody holds.
- **CI, conclusions read personally**: ESLint `success`, TypeScript Type Check `success`, Check Changeset `success`, all Test Core / Dogfood / Temporal shards `success` — 25 checks, zero failures.

**On the structural question I told it to answer rather than skip — it answered by measuring, and filed #7616.** That is the right outcome and worth being explicit about, because "should these endpoints stop re-implementing this resolution?" is the kind of question that normally dies as an unexamined copy. What it established:

- **One rule, three copies**, and it has now drifted **three** times — this card (#7608), #7555 / PR #7605 (an app-declared `isDefault` *displacing* `member_default` instead of composing), and #6334 (grant aggregation missing `sys_user_position` entirely). Each found *after* the divergence reached a user, never at author time.
- **A real de-duplication is a net addition today, not a removal**: `ISecurityService` exposes only `resolvePermissionSetNames` (names), both handlers need full resolved sets; the plugin method is `private`; and the contract *mandates feature-detection*, so the local resolution must stay as a fallback — copy **plus** delegation **plus** a branch. Plus the two resolutions are not the same: `/me/apps` deliberately projects a narrower column set, so delegating is a behaviour change wanting its own measurement.
- And the constraint that would otherwise be rediscovered: `plugin-hono-server` must **not** take a runtime dependency on `plugin-security`, which is optional in these stacks — a service-locator call satisfies that, a package import would not.

#7616 is filed as a `finding` and triage has routed it `domain:spec`, so it is out of this lane. ⛔ Not promoted here. It also flags a stale doc-comment in `plugin-security` describing the second step this PR deletes — outside this PR's file surface, correctly left for whoever takes that card.

Ready flipped, auto-merge armed.
